targets: Collapsing multiple actual source inputs because their chart rules reuse IDs.
Omitting a complete annotation group and silently interpreting it as zero coverage.
Using annotation arrival order and globally repeated IDs to reject or lose later source cases.
Confusing rules on different source pages that share the same rule ID.
Publishing an inventory derived from changed annotation bytes under the old pinned manifest.
Treating an absent upstream domain label as evidence that a business domain is not represented.
Dropping valid chart cases when upstream annotation IDs recur on different inputs.
Reporting uninspected source inputs as covered rather than unknown in the fit assessment.
Declared counters conceal actual successful and failed producing rows.
Observed rows are mistaken for proof of a planned population.
Parser names supply an arbitrary primary order despite unequal scored populations.
Artifact filename or constant identity replaces a hash of the actual retained bytes.
Present-day config/reference files are asserted to establish historical identity.
Current observed configuration overrides the producing historical evidence contract.
Discovery retains only an arbitrary subset and silently drops checkpoints, diagnostics and unreadable artifacts.
Unequal available metric populations are assigned primary ranks without a common declared task population.
